title: Why We Built Another Language App
summary: Parrot CEO Amir Hanna on why he doubted building another language app, and how 52 apps, 65 learner interviews, and a simple MVP changed his mind.
body_markdown:
**“Why would we compete with a 4B giant?” “How did Duolingo make hundreds of millions and still get no one fluent?” “Another language app? Isn’t there thousands of those?”**


Those were my exact questions when my co-founder[Erik Dahl](https://www.parrotapp.com/blog/author/erik-dahl) told me he wanted to build another language app.


At first, I wasn’t convinced. But after working with Erik on a few startups, I knew one thing about him: if he’s obsessed with an idea, it’s probably worth exploring.


Then[Julia Hudea](https://www.parrotapp.com/blog/author/julia-hudea) joined. We met in a university entrepreneurship class at The University of British Columbia. We’d both worked on things that could’ve worked but didn’t matter to us. This one did.


## Before writing any code


Before writing any code, we:


1. Downloaded 52 language learning apps and used every single one for a few hours.
2. Interviewed 65 language learners across Reddit, Discord, and our circles.
3. Found the comprehensible input method, the most research-backed approach to learning a language (listen first, speak later).


## From skepticism to conviction


We built a simple MVP, just a video player with captions, and took it to students. 60% paid for early access. That moment flipped my skepticism into conviction.


Fast forward, Parrot is now growing super fast, joined Y Combinator’s Fall 2025 batch, and some learners are spending 1+ hours on the app.


Julia, Erik, and me at Y Combinator.


What started as doubt turned into a mission: to connect people by breaking down language barriers. To make learning a language feel as natural and addictive as scrolling TikTok.
